evidence: Manual application of check-probe-not-in-seed.py behaviour (private checker not executed; this is a manual review, not a checker run). (1) Every mutation probe in the criteria is either judge-generated with a mandated uniqueness rule or targets records the review itself creates: gate constraints judge.toml hro_gate_shared requires 'a unique title' and 'a unique name, a unique email address'; functional prompt.md line 15 'Use your own new jobs and cards for every board protocol (suffix every title and name for this review)'; polish/visual prompt line 11 'unique title (add a short suffix for this review)'. All board probes (J1/J2 cards A-F, V-Z, reject reasons, notes, activity lines, stale-move F, bulk/undo) live on jobs created in this session, so no seeded card, position, reason or note can satisfy them. Seed has only JOB-PLAT/JOB-DATA/JOB-DSGN, 16 applications, 3 notes on APP-101/107/301, one seeded reject reason on APP-301 (Lena, Product Designer), and no activity table content (db.js seedIfEmpty inserts users/jobs/applications/messages/reads/notes only), so hro_activity and hro_activity_refusals cannot be pre-satisfied. (2) The one literal probe value, polish hro_pol_live_board 'Call back on Fri', is absent (case-insensitive grep) from seed_data.json and from index.html/app.js/board.js/threads.js; the only reference placeholders are 'Reason for rejecting' (board.js:21, 216), so a cleared note box cannot read as the probe. Other polish probes ('a distinctive reply', unsaved note) are judge-chosen. (3) Linking/conversation probes use new records: hro_candidate_linked adds Tomas's email to the new J2 job, distinguishable from his seeded APP-201 Data Analyst application by the unique J2 title; hro_seen, hro_msg_exchange, hro_thread_access, hro_drafts act on that new J2 conversation (no seeded messages or reads); hro_unread_scrolled_up / hro_pol_live_thread use a new Noor message on APP-101 where Rafael's seeded read_count is 120 of 120 (zero unread), so 'one new message' must come from the probe. (4) Seeded values that are read rather than created (Mei Lin's 2 unread on APP-201: 3 messages, read_count 1; Noor's 120-message thread) are baseline readbacks, and the mutating legs are graded relatively ('rises by exactly two'), so they are not pre-satisfied probes. Counterexample attempts: a dead app that never saves notes/reasons/cards cannot pass because the probe text exists nowhere in seed or reference initial state; a conforming alternative is not penalised because no criterion requires a specific seeded collision-free value it cannot produce. Cross-dimension state drift on seeded baselines (e.g. Mei's 2-unread if another dimension opens APP-201) belongs to row 37, not this row.
